title: The continents were once one
sources: Alfred Wegener, The Origin of Continents and Oceans (1915)
NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 4

quiz.q: The Himalaya formed at which type of plate boundary?
quiz.why: Right. Convergent: the Indian plate colliding with the Eurasian plate.

lines.say: Look at a map, and South America seems to fit into Africa.

beats.say: Look at a map, and South America seems to fit into Africa. Alfred Wegener took that seriously.

lines.say: Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, with one supercontinent, Pangaea.
In the 1960s, Harry Hess's sea-floor spreading led to plate tectonics.

beats.say: Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, with one supercontinent, Pangaea. In the 1960s, Harry Hess's sea-floor spreading led to plate tectonics.

lines.say: At divergent boundaries, plates move apart. At convergent ones, they collide, as India did with Asia.
At transform boundaries, they slide past each other.

beats.say: At divergent boundaries, plates move apart. At convergent ones, they collide, as India did with Asia. At transform boundaries, they slide past each other.

lines.say: Wegener's idea was rejected for decades,
because he couldn't explain the force that moved continents.

data.text: He couldn't explain what force moved the continents.
